title: English Vocabulary 2 · Units 05–06
description: Reviewed countries, nationalities, languages, geographic regions, physical features, climate, directions and measurements.
sourceNotice: Vocabulary and curriculum coverage were checked against the user-provided book; example sentences and learning notes are original. Source exercises, long passages, and illustrations are not reproduced.

audit.scope: Presentation pages, tables, figures, exercises 5.1–5.6 and 6.1–6.4, answer key, and available phonemic index checked.
audit.pronunciation: Broad British English IPA informed by the source index where available. Place names and connected-speech variants may have acceptable alternative pronunciations.
audit.languagePolicy: All learning content is in English; Portuguese appears only in the pt translation field.
audit.reviewMethod: Source coverage cross-check, independent lexical and pedagogical review, example/TTS review, schema and import validation.
audit.limitations: Audio and speech-recognition behavior has not been manually tested in the user’s browser.

units.title: Unit 05 — Country, nationality and language
learningObjectives: Match countries with their nationality adjectives and principal languages, recognising that language use can vary within a country.
Use capital letters correctly in names of countries, languages and nationalities.
Use the definite article with the United Kingdom and the United States, and with collective nationality forms such as the British and the Swiss.
Recognise continents and regions, and describe nationality, first language, capitals and population.
Recall relevant country–capital pairs and nationality plurals from the exercises.

units.title: Unit 06 — The physical world
learningObjectives: Identify physical features, including caves, canals, waterfalls, rainforests, oceans and other landforms.
Explain different meanings of cover: a surface, a geographical area and a distance travelled.
Describe temperatures, distances, fractions, heights and depths using common measurement language.
Use climate, landscape, region, consist of and contrast accurately in geographic descriptions.
Locate places with compass points and use source map information in descriptive sentences.

items.example: The Earth moves around the Sun.
items.note: Earth as the name of our planet is normally capitalised; the earth can mean the ground.

items.example: Earth is the planet we live on.
items.note: A large natural object orbiting a star.

items.example: The surface of the lake was still.
items.note: The outer or top part of something.

items.example: Asia is a large continent.
items.note: A major landmass; also studied in Unit 05.

items.note: Land beside the sea.

items.note: A large natural hole or underground space.

items.note: An artificial waterway.

items.example: We walked to a waterfall in the forest.
items.note: Water falling from a high place in a river.

items.note: A forest in a wet, usually tropical, climate.

items.example: The ship crossed the ocean.
items.note: A very large area of salt water.

items.note: The appearance of the land in a particular area.

items.example: We could see a mountain in the distance.
items.note: A high natural area of land.

items.example: The village is beside a lake.
items.note: An inland body of water.

items.example: The river flows through the city.
items.note: Natural flowing water moving towards a lake or sea.

items.example: Very little rain falls in this desert.
items.note: An area with very little precipitation.

items.example: The gardener covered the plants with a sheet.
items.note: A covering is placed over a surface; also use be covered with.

items.example: The ground was covered in leaves.
items.note: Describes a surface with something on it; be covered with is also possible.

items.pt: cobrir uma área; ocupar uma extensão
items.example: The national park covers a large area.
items.note: Here cover describes the extent of something rather than hiding it.

items.example: The cyclists covered a long distance today.
items.note: Here cover means travel through a distance.

items.example: Two thirds of the students chose the first option.
items.note: Fraction: two of three equal parts.

items.example: The bridge is over a hundred years old.
items.note: Here over means more than, not movement above something.

items.example: The cliff is very high.
items.note: Use high for height above the ground.

items.example: The water is deep near the rocks.
items.note: Use deep for the distance down from the top or surface.

items.example: The canal is twenty kilometres long.
items.note: Use long to describe length or distance.

items.example: This is the largest lake in the region.
items.note: Superlative of large.

items.example: That is the highest point on the trail.
items.note: Superlative of high.

items.example: It is the deepest part of the river.
items.note: Superlative of deep.

items.example: This is the longest bridge in the area.
items.note: Superlative of long.

items.example: The wall is three metres high.
items.note: British spelling: metre.

items.example: The town is ten kilometres away.
items.note: British spelling: kilometre.

items.example: The temperature reached thirty degrees Celsius.
items.note: Used to measure temperature.

items.example: It was minus five degrees outside.
items.note: Before a number, minus indicates a value below zero.

items.example: The temperature dropped overnight.
items.note: A measure of how hot or cold something is.

items.example: What is the distance between the two towns?
items.note: The amount of space between places.

items.example: This garden is twice the size of our old one.
items.note: A comparison showing that something is two times as large as another thing.

items.example: We studied geography at school.

items.example: The region has many lakes and hills.

items.example: The group consists of five members.

items.example: There is a clear contrast between the two landscapes.

items.example: The island has a mild climate.
items.note: Usual weather conditions in a region over a long period.

items.example: The area has a Mediterranean climate with dry summers.
items.note: Climate type commonly associated with warm, dry summers and mild, wetter winters.
